1.d4 d5 2.e3 Nf6 3.Bd3.strategy: Develops the bishop to its most active diagonal, aiming at h7, and builds a compact pawn chain, with a later f4 to control e5 and prepare a kingside attack. The price is an inflexible structure, weak light squares and a c1-bishop shut in behind its own pawns.
1.d4 d5 2.e3 Nf6 3.Bd3.name: Queen's Pawn Game: Stonewall Attack
1.d4 d5 2.e3 Nf6 3.Bd3.background: The Stonewall Attack became established in master play after Harry Nelson Pillsbury won all six games in which he used it at the two New York tournaments of 1893. It began to disappear from top-level chess by the early 1920s but remains a popular choice at club level.
